source: Flash Eurobarometer 525, Monitoring the level of financial literacy in the EU (fieldwork Mar-Apr 2023; Poland n=1,003)

quiz.q: Someone puts 100 zl into a savings account with a guaranteed 2% a year. No more payments, no withdrawals. How much is there after five years?
quiz.why: Each year's 2% is added on top of the last, so after five years it is a little over 110 zl.

quiz.q: You will get 1,000 zl in one year, and inflation that year is 2%. With that 1,000 zl, will you be able to buy:
quiz.why: Prices rise 2%, so the same 1,000 zl buys less.

quiz.q: If interest rates rise, what typically happens to bond prices?
quiz.why: New bonds then pay more, so existing bonds become less attractive and their price falls.

quiz.q: An investment with a higher return is likely to be:
options: More risky than one with a lower return
quiz.why: Higher possible returns come with bigger possible swings and losses.

quiz.q: An investment in a wide range of company shares is likely to be:
options: More risky than a single share
Less risky than a single share
quiz.why: Spreading money across many companies means one failure hurts less.

note: Based on Flash Eurobarometer 525 questions Q2-Q6. Amounts shown 1:1 in zl (100 zl, 1,000 zl), no exchange-rate conversion; correct answers are unaffected because they depend only on percentages. Wording slightly shortened for mobile; the exact Polish questionnaire wording was not checked. Present as 'based on the EU's Eurobarometer questions', not as the identical official test. Percentages = % giving the correct answer, from the report's data annex.
